title: Seedling establishment — controlled evidence plan
purpose: Define early seedling establishment, root-zone/environment observation, watering and transplant-readiness evidence without universal stage setpoints.

excludedUntilValidated: feeding recipes detached from media/water/crop context

claims.statement: Seedling establishment should be judged by observed development and root-zone/crop condition rather than age alone because early growth rate varies with genetics and environment.
claims.boundary: Calendar age by itself does not establish transplant readiness.

claims.statement: Young root systems require both water and oxygen, so seedling watering should be interpreted through media moisture, drainage, container size and root-zone condition instead of a fixed schedule.
claims.boundary: The SOP should not prescribe one irrigation volume/frequency across all media and containers.

claims.statement: Temperature and humidity/VPD influence plant water relations, but research treatment values should be used as evidence of relationships rather than universal seedling setpoints.
claims.boundary: Facility crop plans and measured crop response govern operational setpoints.

claims.statement: Seedling abnormalities such as collapse, discoloration or poor roots should trigger an evidence-based differential that includes water/oxygen, environment, injury and disease rather than an automatic single diagnosis.
claims.boundary: Visual symptoms alone are insufficient to confirm a specific pathogen or nutrient cause.

claims.statement: Transplant readiness records should preserve seed/plant identity, developmental condition, root-zone status, abnormal findings and destination so weak or suspect plants are not silently mixed into healthy cohorts.
claims.boundary: Exact acceptance criteria require facility validation for the chosen container, medium and crop plan.
